 Judgment
The appellant is the claimant before the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal (Mact), Thrissur.
The appellant met with an accident on 19.09.2013, when he was 62 years of age.
A claim for Rs.3,00,000/- was made before the MACT, and by the impugned award, the learned Tribunal granted Rs.1,87,710/-.
It is against the afore award that the captioned appeal is filed by the appellant.

2. Heard Sri.Nimod, learned counsel for the appellant, and Smt. Archana, learned counsel for the 3rd respondent Insurance company.
3.
The challenge in this appeal is essentially against the fixation of the monthly income of the appellant at Rs.6,500/- per month, notionally.

The appellant claims that he was an agriculturist, and admittedly, there was no evidence as regards the monthly income claimed by him at Rs.10,000/-
before the MACT.

In this regard, this Court notices the judgment of the Apex Court in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal MACA NO.919 OF 2021 2025:KER:58947 Sundaram Alliance Insurance Company Limited [(2011) 13 SCC 236], as per which, the notional income requires to be fixed at Rs.9,000/- per month.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: When that be so, I am of the opinion that the monthly income requires to be fixed at Rs.9,000/- per month.

4. Though the learned counsel for the appellant sought to contend that the claim for loss of amenities as well as pain and sufferings, etc., also requires to be considerably enhanced, taking into account the nature of the injuries suffered by the appellant, I am of the opinion that the amount granted by the MACT, cannot be said to be insufficient.

5. In such circumstances, the appellant would be entitled for the following amounts:

Resultantly, the appeal would stand partially allowed, the impugned award is modified, entitling the claimants to get a total compensation of Rs.35,200/- (Rupees Thirty five thousand two hundred only) after deducting the amount already awarded by the Tribunal with interest at 7% per annum from the date of the petition till realization and proportionate costs.
